gaps.needs: For every commutative A supply the enhanced Habiro reflection with its factorial and divisibility towers, tensor and cyclotomic homotopy detection, exactly as specified below.
For every A and m>0 supply coherent finite cyclotomic complete descent, its arithmetic fracture, mapping spaces, divisor restriction and coefficient naturality as specified below.
For perfectly covered A and étale R/A supply the static marked stages E_m, their ghost and Frobenius transitions and static complete limit, with the specified uniqueness and reduction equivalences.

For a Λ-map between perfectly covered A and A′ and a compatible map from étale R/A to étale R′/A′, prove that the completed coefficient Frobenius maps commute with the induced prime-completed map, including the linearization coherences.
For m>1 prove that the ideal of ℤ[q] generated by the q-integers [p] at q^(m/p), for primes p dividing m, equals (Φ_m); at m=1 retain the separate empty ideal (0).

Supply the light solid spectral category, null-sequence generator, product tensor, split finite free tower and balanced-base-change comparisons, countable-limit/ω₁-filtered-colimit interchange, null-family formula and uniformly bounded-below simplicial realization compatibility stated above.
For R=𝒪_F[1/Δ] with Δ>0 divisible by disc(F), supply the ordinary GSWZ ring with its full cyclotomic coefficient algebras, Taylor maps and completed Frobenius gluing.
For Δ>0 divisible by 6 and disc(F), supply actual K₃(F)-indexed global invertible modules over the GSWZ ring, effective descent, unit and inverse pairings and coherent multiplication equivalences.
For the global indexed lines with Δ divisible by 6 and disc(F), supply their integral order-one evaluation over 𝒪_F[1/Δ] and a section evaluating to 1, compatible with the unit and tensor pairings.

For F→E and a common positive Δ divisible by 6 and both discriminants, supply scalar equivalences of the actual indexed global lines respecting restriction on K₃, pairings, Taylor maps and integral order-one evaluation, with identity and composition coherences.
